text:
Mira: Quick heads-up — after last night's kernel selector update, canary shows long sequences taking >40% more of the batch token budget and short sequences getting delayed. Full trace in dashboard: https://redwood.dev/dash/epoch-batch/2873 :frowning:
Aj: Saw that. Looks like our token_budget_target calc shifted when kernel favored the fastpath for certain attention shapes, so mini-batch formation prefers long seqs and drains the queue faster for them.
Mira: Any quick mitigations? We have a couple customers reporting tail-latency regressions on chat flows.
Kai: Two short-term options: (1) cap per-request token_credit to a fraction of epoch_budget; (2) implement epoch-rotation so short-seq lanes get guaranteed admission slots every N windows.
Aj: Prototype cap I tried locally: ```python
# pseudo
per_request_cap = min(global_budget * 0.25, seq_len * 2)
```
Dropped from 0.5 -> 0.25 in the experiment and saw short admission improve.
Dahlia: We should also validate KV cache hit bias — long sequences warm KV and then get more beneficial batching. Add KV-hit-by-tenant and KV-hit-by-seqlen telemetry.
runtime-bot: deploybot: rollout started for epoch-batcher-v2 canary (nodes: batch-stage-3), build 2026.03.17-8.
Mira: OK run canary with token cap 0.25 and rotation window 10s. Add trace-id header to requests so we can correlate kernel selection -> batch outcome.
Henry: Also enable kernel-fallback-on-starve = true for the canary so extremely long requests don't block short lanes.
Aj: Telemetry patch pushed: added fields epoch_id, queue_pos, pre_batch_kv_hit (0/1), kernel_suggest. Will land in canary in ~5min.
Kai: Need defined success criteria: p95 tail latency <= baseline + 5ms, short-seq admission rate >= 95%, KV-hit variance < 10% of baseline.
Dahlia: Can we snapshot KV cache distribution pre/post? I can add a nightly job to sample tenant KV occupancy and top-k warmed keys.
Mira: Deployment plan: if canary stable for 2h, ramp 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 48h. Auto-rollback if short_seq_admit < 90% on any step.
runtime-bot: metric-alert: canary p99 latency spike +18ms on batch-stage-3 — triggered at 2873012458.
Aj: Likely due to kernel fastpath mismatch with quantized matmul kernel selection. I'll toggle kernel-fallback and re-run short load.
Mira: Good. Also log per-tenant token_consumed_per_epoch so we can detect noisy neighbors automatically.
Henry: FYI i reproduced locally with stress mix (80% short / 20% long). Snippet: ```sh
w rk -c200 -d60 --seq-mix "short:80,long:20"
```
Kai: Agree we should add a per-tenant fairness_score metric and an automatic hedging policy: if fairness_score < 0.8 then enable rotation for that tenant.
Dahlia: I'll own dashboard tiles + alert thresholds. Will post the new dashboard link when tiles are ready.
Mira: Thanks all — let's reconvene in 30m in #eng-runtime if canary still alive. :thumbsup:
Aj: Added a unit test to simulate KV-warmup skew and pushed to CI.
runtime-bot: ci/canary passed, integration tests failed for kernel-fallback (non-blocking).
Mira: Keep me posted, will follow up after the 30m check-in.
